title: Viva Engage: sensitivity labels for communities (Microsoft Purview)
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing quotations and listed commands are supported. The deletion guidance omits Microsoft's required check that a label is no longer visible before deleting it, which matters because deleting a still-published container label can cause creation failures.

claims.claim: The roadmap says organisations can manually apply Information Protection sensitivity labels in Engage.
claims.quote: Your organization can now manually apply Information Protection sensitivity labels in Engage.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators create labels and publishing policies to determine which users and groups can manually label content in Engage.
claims.quote: Sensitivity label support in this new application will allow admins to create labels and configure label publishing policies to determine which users and groups can manually label content in Engage.

claims.claim: End users can label Engage communities to classify and protect data through privacy and external user access controls.
claims.quote: End users will be able to manually apply labels to Engage communities and in turn classify and protect their sensitive data via privacy and external user access controls.

claims.claim: Learn documents applying labels configured with associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal to Engage communities.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Container sensitivity labels must be enabled and configured before users can apply them to supported containers, including Engage communities.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them. These include Microsoft team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in because administrators must enable and configure container labels and publish them for users.
claims.quote: Until sensitivity labels are enabled for containers, the settings are visible but you can't configure them.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Labels are not available to select in apps or services until published in a label policy.
claims.quote: Until you publish your labels, they won't be available to select in apps or for services. To publish the labels, they must be added to a label policy.

claims.claim: Enabling container sensitivity labels is a one-time procedure.
claims.quote: If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure:

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A container label set to Public or Private sets and locks privacy until the sensitivity label is removed.
claims.quote: The settings of Public or Private set and lock the privacy setting when you apply this label to the container.

claims.claim: The label's External user access setting controls whether owners can add guests to communities.
claims.quote: External user access: Control whether the owner can add guests to the container, similar to Manage guest access in Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Communities created with a label disallowing guest access are available only to users in the organisation.
claims.quote: Communities created with a label that doesn’t allow guest access are only available to users in your organization. People outside your organization can’t be added to the community.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Items inside labelled containers do not inherit the container label.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Container labels do not apply item-level content markings or encryption.
claims.quote: If the label's scope includes files and emails, other label settings such as encryption and content marking aren't applied to the items within the container.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An administrator can choose a default Engage community label as part of Microsoft Purview label policy settings.
claims.quote: As an example, select a preferred default label for Engage communities in Microsoft Purview as part of label policy settings.

claims.claim: The Engage default takes precedence over the site default and can be more permissive.
claims.quote: This new default takes precedence over the default label for sites.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The configured default sensitivity label applies automatically when a user creates a community.
claims.quote: Admins can set up sensitivity labels to automatically apply during community creation. When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The community creator can select another available label.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: The user creating a community cannot create new sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: Community admins change labels through community > More (...) > Settings and the Engage and site default dropdowns.
claims.quote: Open the community, select the More menu (...), and choose Settings. ... choose the General label as your Engage default label and the Public label as your site default.

claims.claim: Users see the sensitivity label in the live community's banner.
claims.quote: After the community is live, the sensitivity label appears to users in the community banner:

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn says PowerShell cmdlets do not directly support sensitivity labels for Engage communities.
claims.quote: Before you use sensitivity labels for Engage, PowerShell cmdlets don't directly support sensitivity labels. Users can't directly specify sensitivity labels for Engage communities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: PowerShell can label the connected SharePoint site as a workaround that updates the existing Engage community's label.
claims.quote: As a workaround, you can use PowerShell to apply labels to a SharePoint site that connects to an existing Engage community. Doing so causes the label on the Engage community to correspondingly update.

claims.claim: The Viva compliance overview still says sensitivity labels are unsupported in Viva Engage, unlike the feature documentation.
claims.quote: The Viva Engage features eDiscovery and Data Retention are supported by Microsoft Purview; sensitivity labels and data loss prevention aren't supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Engage as a public-first platform in many organisations.
claims.quote: Engage is a public-first platform in many organizations.

claims.claim: Learn recommends Public for access by anyone in the organisation and illustrates a Public Engage default.
claims.quote: Privacy: Keep the default of Public if you want anyone in your organization to access the container where this label is applied.

claims.claim: Clearing External user access changes access for new users, not existing guests.
claims.quote: The new setting applies to new users but not to existing users. For example, if this setting was previously selected and as a result, guest users accessed the site, these guest users can still access the site after this setting is cleared in the label configuration.

claims.claim: Publishing external sharing and authentication context label settings can let site owners change settings otherwise restricted to administrators.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft says to allow 24 hours for label and policy changes to propagate before troubleshooting.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against changing applied labels' site and group settings and says to wait at least 24 hours if they are changed.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites. If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.

claims.claim: The Entra documentation says published group-setting changes are not automatically applied to labelled groups.
claims.quote: When you make changes to group settings for a published label in the Microsoft Purview portal, those policy changes aren't automatically applied on the labeled groups.

claims.claim: Entra documentation directs administrators to manually apply unavoidable group-label setting updates using a PowerShell script.
claims.quote: If you must make a change, use a PowerShell script to manually apply updates to the affected groups. This method makes sure that all existing groups enforce the new setting.

claims.claim: Deleting a site-and-group label still included in policies can cause creation failures for teams, groups and sites.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label that has the site and group settings enabled, and that label is included in one or more label policies, this action can result in creation failures for new teams, groups, and sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The deletion guidance tells administrators to remove a label from every policy and wait at least one hour before deleting it, without verifying that it is no longer visible.
claims.quote: After this wait period, try creating a team, group, or site and confirm that the label is no longer visible. ... If the sensitivity label isn't visible, you can now safely delete the label.
claims.fix: In both deletion instructions, say: 'Remove the label from every label policy, wait at least one hour, then try creating a team, group, or site and confirm that the label is no longer visible. Delete the label only if it is no longer visible.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites#deleting-published-labels-that-are-configured-for-sites-and-groups.

claims.claim: Users need an appropriate sensitivity-label licence.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels reaches the page holding label configuration.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: The path correctly stops on the labels page. Extend it for a classic label scheme to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create a label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites > Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > Privacy and external user access'. For a modern label scheme, replace '+ Create a label' with '+ Create > Label'. The last wizard steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites, already cited.

claims.claim: The printed New-Label call creates a Site, UnifiedGroup label with enabled site/group protection and the specified Public/Private and Boolean guest-access settings.
claims.quote: Valid values are: ... Site ... UnifiedGroup ... Values can be combined ... SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled ... $true ... SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy ... Public ... Private ... SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers ... $true ... $false

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies reaches the page holding label publishing policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... On the Label policies page, select Publish label ... On the Choose sensitivity labels to publish page, select the Choose sensitivity labels to publish link.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Choose sensitivity labels to publish'. This reaches the label-selection control documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels#publish-sensitivity-labels-by-creating-a-label-policy.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a policy containing the named labels in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote:
New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management"
This example creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.claim: The table's New-Label and New-LabelPolicy calls create labels and policies, not community assignments, and the shown policy call does not choose recipients or a container default.
claims.quote: Use the New-LabelPolicy cmdlet to create sensitivity label policies in your organization. ... The Labels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that are associated with the policy.
